A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Label Horizon Paradox study and bi-level framework. All pages, including Appendices A–F, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables that support matching retained material and identifying additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments across three CSI indices and ten architectures, horizon sweeps, label-selection analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds S&P 500 forecasting, CSI 500 market-stress evaluation and downstream portfolio backtesting.

M1.justification: The softmax horizon weights, bi-level losses, entropy regularization, warm-up and single-step inner update are retained. v4 explicitly states that the forecasting model is retrained on the selected horizon; selected-label training was already described in v1 Section 5.1 and Appendix E.2, so this clarifies the procedure rather than establishing a new component.

E1.justification: v4 adds daily forecasting on US S&P 500 stocks, a CSI 500 test scenario covering the February 2024 crash, and a portfolio task using predictions before market close. These substantially extend the market and operating conditions beyond v1's retained CSI interday and intraday forecasting coverage.

E2.justification: The same ten backbone architectures and standard-training comparators remain. Naive Averaging, Equal-Weight MTL and their selected-top-five variants are also retained. The new experiments use the existing backbone set; the added label-smoothing discussion does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include 390-minute US sessions represented by 26 patches, an earlier chronological split for the crash-period test, and a separate top-20% portfolio backtest with predictions 15 minutes before close, subsequent 10-minute TWAP execution and trading frictions. The original top-10% signal metrics remain. Sections 5.1 and A.5 also change the reported optimizer from Adam to AdamW, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E.4 adds a stress analysis of performance during a severe downturn and crash. Appendix E.5 tests whether predictive benefits translate into portfolio outcomes under execution constraints and trading frictions. The existing warm-up, learned-weight and label-aggregation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing five-seed averaging practice and individual-trial horizon plots remain unchanged. The new US and stress-test tables repeat the five-seed practice; no new confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v4 Tables 6–8 add US-market, stress-test and portfolio results. For example, the new US LSTM comparison reports IC (×10) of 0.314 for standard training and 0.459 for the proposed framework. Tables 1–5 and the runtime table, renumbered from Table 6 to Table 9, retain their numerical entries; the additions are not improvements over earlier same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Appendix C generalizes the signal amplitude beyond normalization to one, carries alpha(Delta) through the performance derivation, and adds a general multiplicative correction in v4 Equation 44 before recovering the interday approximation. It also explicitly specifies joint Brownian noise across horizons. These refine the existing factor-model analysis while preserving its principal derivative criterion and partial-correlation proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central label-horizon claim remain stable, but the introduction's empirical contribution expands to claim cross-market generalizability, resilience during macroeconomic shocks and practical profitability. This substantially broadens v1's claims about forecasting improvements, particularly because v1 explicitly placed complete trading-strategy evaluation outside its scope.

C2.justification: v4 interprets US results through faster information incorporation and stress-test results as evidence of risk resilience. Appendix B.2 replaces v1's extended backtesting caveat with discussion of practical economic evaluation. Appendix C.1 also newly acknowledges that the theory fixes the signal direction across horizons and excludes factor rotations.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly documents selected-horizon retraining, US session and input dimensions, additional chronological splits, and portfolio selection and execution rules. Existing warm-up duration, bi-level learning rates and hardware information remain. No code-access instructions are added, and numerical transaction-cost and slippage assumptions remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v4 adds a focused distinction from label smoothing, citing Müller et al. (2019), and adds forecasting reviews by Shah et al. (2022) and Sonkavde et al. (2023). Rahaman et al. (2019) is removed. The principal positioning relative to sample reweighting remains; publication updates for existing citations do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: Substantial prose rewrites and expansions affect the contribution list, baseline explanations, main-results narrative, warm-up discussion, related work and conclusion. The Software and Data disclosure is merged into the Impact Statement. These changes considerably reshape the explanatory narrative despite retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: v4 adds three substantial comparison tables covering US forecasting, market stress and portfolio outcomes. Figure 4 is redrawn with a different color scheme and relocated, while Table 5 and the runtime table also move. Figures 1–3 and the original tables retain their principal display structures.

improvement.justification: The US and crash-period experiments strengthen evidence that the findings extend beyond the original market and test window, while Appendix C clarifies the decomposition's assumptions and approximation. These gains are tempered by stronger profitability and resilience claims than the reporting fully supports: friction rates are unspecified, and Table 8 includes an annual-return decline for Bi-Mamba+ from 39.40% to 39.17%. The net improvement is useful but limited.
